The Big Story
US economy grew 3.4%

lines.say: The economy grew three point four percent. Feel it?

lines.text: That's the first official estimate for July through September, and it beat forecasts.
lines.say: That's the first official estimate for July through September, and it beat forecasts.

lines.text: It's a jump from 2.5% in the first quarter and 2.2% in the second.
lines.say: It's a jump from two point five percent in the first quarter and two point two percent in the second.

lines.text: Shoppers did a lot of the work. Consumer spending grew at a 3.8% pace.
lines.say: Shoppers did a lot of the work. Consumer spending grew at a three point eight percent pace.

lines.text: AP reports AI investment by businesses was another big push.
lines.say: AP reports AI investment by businesses was another big push.

lines.text: But a separate report shows prices still running hot. The Fed's favorite inflation gauge was up 3.6% in September from a year earlier.
lines.say: But a separate report shows prices still running hot. The Fed's favorite inflation gauge was up three point six percent in September from a year earlier.

lines.text: Here's the catch. GDP measures the whole economy's output after inflation, not your paycheck or your grocery bill.

lines.text: So a strong economy and a tight budget can both be true. And this is only estimate one of three.

post.title: The economy grew 3.4%. Why doesn't it feel like it?
post.ig:
The US economy grew 3.4%. So why doesn't it feel like it?
Real GDP grew at a 3.4% annual rate in Q3 2026, up from 2.2% in Q2 (BEA advance estimate, Oct 29, 2026).
Consumer spending grew at a 3.8% pace, and AI investment helped too.
But in a separate report, the Fed's favorite inflation gauge was up 3.6% in September from a year earlier.
This is the first of three estimates.
Sources: BEA, CNBC, AP.
News and education, not financial advice.
